Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Equilibrium pilot

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the call this morning — we left with a clear ask from our side: we need a tight sizing recommendation for the dedicated pilot (US region) so our platform team can sign off with procurement. A few specifics from our side:

- Target SLA: p95 inference latency <= 350ms (tail important for UX flows)
- Peak patterns: 1 major spike window (09:00–11:00 PT) and a broad evening plateau (18:00–22:00 PT)
- Expected request mix: 65% chat-style prompts, 35% batch generation; median prompt length ~120 tokens, average generation length ~90 tokens
- Expected QPS during peak day-of-launch: ~1100 requests/minute sustained for 15–30 minutes, with microbursts up to 2200 reqs/minute for 2–3 minutes

Attached is a sample of our production traffic trace (Equilibrium-prod-load-sample.csv).

Can you provide a tokens/sec estimate mapped to GPUs (we're open to quantized variants), recommended headroom to maintain p95 <=350ms, and a proposed commit/burst strategy we can include in our PO? Also, timeline: we want to onboard in mid-August (canary + 2-week ramp).

Cc-ing procurement for visibility (procurement@equilibrium.ai).

Best,

Head of Platform
Equilibrium Labs

Naomi / Karthik — quick model back. See attached workbook (throughput-estimates-07011.xlsx) for the microcalc. TL;DR recommendations below (assumptions at end).

Summary recommendation (pilot phase / US region):
- Recommended model: Llama-2-70B trimmed + 8-bit quant (verified perf profile)
- Per-GPU sustained serving throughput (steady chat mix): ~380K tokens/minute (~6333 tokens/sec) on H100-80 (with continuous batching, prefix KV cache enabled)
- Typical request (120 in + 90 gen = 210 tokens total) -> ~30 requests/min per GPU sustained (chat conversions considered)

SLO mapping & headroom:
- At 1100 reqs/min peak (their ask) -> ~37 GPUs needed to hit p95 <= 350ms (steady-state assumptions + batching benefits)
- For 2x microburst (2200 reqs/min for short spikes) -> recommend burst buffer = 18 additional GPUs (schedule autoscale to add within 30–60s). That gives ~55 GPUs total during burst windows and should hold p95 under 350ms for bursts <5 min.
- Safety/headroom: recommend baseline commit = 45 GPUs for pilot (this provides ~20% steady-state headroom vs modeled peak and a gradual buffer for warmups). Burst policy: +20 GPUs on policy trigger for observed queue depth or token backlog.

Latency caveats:
- p95 numbers assume warmed KV caches and active continuous batching with target batching window 15–30ms. Cold-warm scenarios (first 10–15 minutes post-deploy) could see p95 increases ~1.4x unless pre-warmed cache is run.
- If you require p99 tighter than 600ms, we recommend bumping baseline commit +10 GPUs or using HBM-optimized kernels with slightly higher cost.

Cost/ops notes:
- H100-80 is recommended for predictable tail latency at scale; A100-80 shows ~12–18% lower tokens/sec at p95 on our benchmarks for the quant config chosen.
- Consider reserved commit for pilot month and a short-term burst credit bucket for production launch to avoid procurement friction.

Assumptions (high level):
- Model execution profile based on L2-70B quant perf measured on Redwood internal bench (seq_len 256 / kv caching warm, gen 90 tokens)
- Average token compute cost = bench-derived composite; network/transfer negligible for this sizing (hosted in same cloud region)
- Batching effectiveness: continuous batching with adaptive windows, effective concurrency utilized 70% of theoretical max during peak

Next steps I propose:
1) Naomi / Karthik review and approve numbers — I'll tidy into a one-page technical appendix for procurement.
2) Draft MAP (mutual action plan) + canary runway: 2-week canary at 20% traffic, then full launch.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
